entries.keywords: budget budgeting money plan income expenses spend save household
entries.a: A simple budget: write down your income, list needs first (food, rent, transport, school fees), then wants, and put some money aside before you spend. Check weekly. If spending is more than income, cut wants first.

entries.keywords: emergency fund savings save little by little rainy day
entries.a: Build an emergency fund by saving a small amount every time you are paid, even a little. Aim for a few months of basic costs. Keep it separate from daily spending money.

entries.keywords: start small business idea customers profit selling tuckshop side hustle
entries.a: To start a small business: pick something people near you need, test with a few customers, count your costs, set a price above cost, and keep records of what comes in and goes out. Profit = money earned minus costs.

entries.keywords: pricing price product markup profit margin cost selling price
entries.a: Pricing: add up all costs for one item (materials, transport, your time), then add a profit on top. Example: costs $3, you want $2 profit, so sell at $5. Check what others charge, but do not sell below cost.

entries.keywords: record keeping cash book accounts bookkeeping receipts business records
entries.a: Keep a cash book: date, what happened, money in, money out, balance. Keep receipts. Good records show whether you really make a profit and help you get loans.

entries.keywords: scam scams fraud mobile money phishing fake message pin password online safety
entries.a: Scam safety: never share your PIN, password or one-time code, even with someone claiming to be the bank or mobile money agent. Be careful of messages saying you won a prize or must pay to receive money. Stop, check with the real company, and tell someone you trust.

entries.keywords: parent help child learn homework support reading together routine
entries.a: Helping a child learn: read together for 10 to 15 minutes a day, ask 'what do you think will happen?', keep a quiet homework time, praise effort, and let them explain their answer to you. Mistakes are part of learning.

entries.keywords: adult learner learn to read adults study again late learning older
entries.a: You are never too old to learn. Start with short daily practice, use words you see in real life (signs, labels, messages), and build up. The lessons here work for anyone; begin at the level that feels comfortable.

entries.keywords: teacher teaching lesson planning classroom ideas use platform with class
entries.a: For teachers: use the lessons and quizzes as a starter or revision activity, set a quiz and review the results together, and use the Project Writer for class projects. Adapt everything to your syllabus.

entries.keywords: stress mental health wellbeing worried anxious sleep talk support
entries.a: When stress builds up: breathe slowly, sleep enough, move your body, and talk to someone you trust. If you feel unsafe or hopeless, speak to a doctor, counsellor or trusted person. In Zimbabwe, children can call Childline on 116.

entries.keywords: when to go clinic doctor sick fever health advice medical
entries.a: I give general information only. For fever that lasts, severe pain, breathing problems, or any worry about health, go to a clinic or doctor. In an emergency, get help immediately instead of waiting.

entries.keywords: home garden grow food vegetables nutrition family kitchen garden
entries.a: A small kitchen garden can feed a family: grow leafy greens, tomatoes and onions, add compost, water at the cool times of day, and cover soil with mulch. Save seeds from your best plants.
